title: Cohen–Macaulay loci and arbitrary field extension
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $X$ a locally finite-type $k$-scheme, and $K/k$ any field extension. Write $p:X_K=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ for the projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. A point $x'\in X_K$ with image $x$ belongs to the Cohen–Macaulay locus of $X_K$ if and only if $x$ belongs to the Cohen–Macaulay locus of $X$. Here Cohen–Macaulay at a point means that the depth of the Noetherian local ring equals its Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-depth], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

Consequently, if $f:X\to S$ is a locally finite-type morphism of Noetherian schemes, the relative Cohen–Macaulay locus $U_f$, consisting of points $x$ at which the local ring of the ordinary fibre $X_{f(x)}$ is Cohen–Macaulay, is also the locus obtained by testing geometric fibres. For any base change $S'\to S$ with $S'$ Noetherian, the relative Cohen–Macaulay locus of $f':X\times_SS'\to S'$ is the inverse image of $U_f$. No perfectness of the residue fields and no separability or finite-generation assumption on $K/k$ is required.

Here a Noetherian scheme admits a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings, and a ring is Noetherian when every ideal is finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].
